sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Wichita Falls?
sections.html:
A Wichita Falls tax bill passes through three hands. Appraisal district staff decide what your property is worth and rule on exemptions and protests. Elected boards at the city, the county and Wichita Falls ISD each pick a rate. Then the Wichita County Tax Office mails the bill and takes the money, covering 8 taxing jurisdictions and sending out almost $120 million in its latest tax year.

Wichita Falls has 101,951 residents, a little below the 2010 count of 104,553. A typical owner-occupied home is worth about $156,800, so the $140,000 school exemption wipes out most of the school value on a house at that price.

  • Value, exemption or protest questions: Wichita Appraisal District, P.O. Box 5172, Wichita Falls, 76307, (940) 322-2435, open on weekdays from 8:00am until 5:00pm.
  • Bills and payment: Wichita County Tax Office.
  • City budget and rate hearings: the City of Wichita Falls.

The city's 2026 rate is $0.677900 for every $100 of taxable value, a small drop from $0.682500. Wichita County is at $0.518590 and Wichita Falls ISD at $1.034677. Rates in nearby towns went different ways, so if you are weighing a move across town, compare complete bills, school line included.

Inside the city figure, $0.652925 pays for day-to-day operations and $0.024975 pays down debt. Two benchmark rates frame it: $0.666037 is the no-new-revenue rate, and $0.717729 is the voter-approval rate. Go over the first and the same houses pay more total tax than the year before. Stay under the second and no election is needed. Wichita Falls lands between them. School debt is a large slice of the ISD rate: $0.359277 of the $1.034677.

Burkburnett city went from $0.678251 to $0.758386, and Iowa Park stayed at $0.694500 both years. Ask the county tax office for the combined rate on your own account.

Pay by January 31. If a balance is still open on February 1 it becomes delinquent, with a 6% penalty and 1% interest added that day. The penalty then gains a point each month and tops out at 12% on July 1. Interest has no ceiling. Owners who are seniors, disabled, or disabled veteran homeowners may split the bill into four payments.

  • Early spring: appraisal notices start arriving, around April 1 for single-family homesteads.
  • May 15: usual protest deadline, pushed later when notices come late.
  • July 25: the chief appraiser hands the certified roll to every taxing unit.
  • October: bills are mailed and payable on receipt.
  • January 31: final day without late charges.

The tax office follows the Wichita Falls ISD schedule for weather closures, so check before driving downtown on a bad-weather day near the deadline.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and other ways to lower the bill
sections.html:
Start with the residence homestead exemption, then protest the appraisal if the value looks too high. The appraisal district takes both. File exemption paperwork before May 1 in most cases.

Every residence homestead gets a $140,000 break on the school district value, and seniors and disabled owners get another $60,000. Nothing applies by itself in most cases: you file, and the chief appraiser decides whether the property qualifies. Local governments and colleges can layer on exemptions of their own, in percent or dollars. Ask the appraisal district which ones the city and county chose.

  • Disabled veteran exemptions run from $5,000 for a rating of 10% to 29% up to $12,000 for 70% to 100%. A veteran rated 100% disabled can receive a total exemption on a residence homestead.
  • After a homestead exemption has been held a year, its appraised value can grow no more than 10% annually.
  • Older and disabled owners may freeze the school district tax on their home.
  • In certain cases a widow or widower aged 55 or older keeps the late spouse's over-65 benefits.

Lose at the review board and you still have district court or binding arbitration. Keep paying the tax nobody disputes while the case moves.

The city rate has drifted down: $0.694321 for 2022, $0.680000 for 2023, $0.684800 for 2024, $0.682500 for 2025 and $0.677900 for 2026. Wichita Falls ISD fell faster, from $1.296500 in 2022 to $1.034677 in 2026, and Wichita County slid from $0.560400 to $0.518590.

All three rates have fallen, so a larger bill usually traces to a higher taxable value rather than a higher rate. On a qualifying home the 10% annual cap limits that rise. Rental and other non-homestead property gets no such cap.

Before you list, make one call. If your appraisal notice jumped by more than the cap allows, phone the appraisal district at (940) 322-2435 and confirm the homestead exemption is on file. Without it the full school value stays on your bill.

The lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1. That puts the bill on whoever owned the house that day, even if you sell in March, and the seller settles it at closing. Delinquent tax left on the account keeps the buyer from getting clear title.

  1. Request a tax statement for each unit from the county tax office before you list.
  2. Give the statements to the title company so it can add up what is owed.
  3. Closing pays the balance out of your sale proceeds.
  4. File the paid receipt with your closing papers.

Heirs who inherit a house but are not named on the recorded deed can still claim the exemption. They bring an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a utility bill.

Once a bill is delinquent, the collector sends notices, may set up a payment plan, and can file suit, with court costs piled on top. A tax foreclosure sale is an auction run by the constable or by an agent the unit hires. Former owners get a limited right to buy the property back, and the window is longer for homestead, agricultural and mineral property.

Back taxes do not rule out a sale. Your title company pays the balance out of the proceeds, and the buyer gets a clean account. A cash sale also skips the lender appraisal and repair requests, which helps when time is short. Call the tax office for a payoff figure first. Then you know the full delinquent amount, with penalty and interest, before you weigh any offer. If the account has gone to a lawsuit, ask whether a payment plan is on file and bring that paper to the title company too.

faqs.q: What is the Wichita Falls city tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The city adopted $0.677900 per $100 of taxable value, down from $0.682500 for tax year 2025.

faqs.q: When are Wichita County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1. Unpaid tax then carries a 6% penalty and 1% interest, and the penalty rises monthly to 12% by July.
The Wichita Appraisal District, at (940) 322-2435 or cs@wadtx.com, weekdays 8:00am to 5:00pm. Call it about values, exemptions and protests.

faqs.q: How much school exemption does a homestead get?
faqs.a: $140,000 off the school district value on a residence homestead, plus another $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners. You must apply, usually before May 1.

faqs.q: Did Wichita Falls rates go down this year?
faqs.a: Yes, for the city, county and school district. The city went from 0.682500 to 0.677900 and Wichita Falls ISD from 1.075287 to 1.034677.
